summary: Feed s163_triple is degraded: IDS missing both directions (17.3% one-way sessions) and 5.4% TCP packet loss impairs detection, plus 17.8% duplicates waste capacity. Tool requires both directions and full payload.

findings.root_cause: Asymmetric visibility - only one direction of TCP sessions is delivered to the IDS. Likely uplink/downlink or east/west SPANs are not aggregated to the same tool port, or a hash-based load-balancer is splitting client->server and server->client across different outputs.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs both directions for TCP reassembly and state tracking. With 24 of 139 sessions (17.3%) one-way, it cannot reconstruct flows, misses bidirectional attack patterns, creates false one-way alerts and incomplete session logs.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS port using bidirectional 5-tuple hashing so TCP reassembly and detection work correctly.

findings.root_cause: Packet loss in the visibility path - 121 of 2231 TCP packets (5.4%) show gaps/retransmissions indicating drops. Tool overload is healthy, so drops are likely SPAN oversubscription or packet broker buffer exhaustion during bursts before the IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for signature and anomaly detection. Missing packets break reassembly, cause missed exploits, truncated files and unreliable flow records; IDS will fail to detect attacks hidden in dropped segments.

recommended_fix.why: Reduce loss by replacing oversubscribed SPAN with TAP where possible and load-balancing flows bidirectionally across IDS capacity to eliminate broker drops while preserving both directions.

findings.root_cause: Overlapping capture points feeding the same tool port without deduplication - 419 of 2354 packets (17.8%) are duplicates, typical when the same traffic is tapped/SPANned at multiple points and aggregated.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU/storage processing the same packet twice, inflates connection counts and alerts, skews analytics and can mask true throughput leading to false capacity planning.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet broker deduplication to strip identical packets within a short window before delivery, giving the IDS a single correct copy of each packet.
